gruss_morgen.text: Morning, young sprout. Mornings used to be earlier back in the day. Noon started at six.

gruss_tag.text: Alwin. Retired rancher. Retirement means I now do my resting standing up.

gruss_abend.text: Nice evening. We had those in my day too. They were bigger though, the evenings.

gruss_regen.text: You call that rain? Back in the day the rain fell bottom to top. We had to hold our umbrellas upside down.

gruss_freund.text: Well, if it isn't my favorite whippersnapper. Sit on the fence. The spot next to me is reserved. For you.

optionen.text: Tell me about the old days!
Tell me about the old days!
Tell me about the old days!

text: Back in the day, we had nothing. Not even hay. We combed the grass blade by blade.
The horses thought it was silly. But it did look tidy.
Did I tell you about the great drought? Three summers without a drop. The pond was just an idea.
Last time I told it, it was two summers. Good stories grow with you, you know.
You know what the best thing about the old days was? Nothing. The best is now, with you fixing this place up.
Don't spread it around. If word gets out that I'm praising the present, I'll lose my license as an old man.

quest_vergabe.text: Got a thing. My bones say no, but the thing needs doing. Your bones are younger.

quest_annahme.text: Good sprout. Back in the day this would've taken three people. And a donkey. The donkey was the smart one.

ablehnung.text: Understood. Hurry was never my pace. I once took two years to answer a question. The answer was: maybe.

quest_abgabe.text: Well, would you look at that. Clean. In my day we'd have thrown a party for this. We still will. Here's your share.

geschenk_liebt.text: Hay. Smell it. SMELL it! That's the scent of fifty good years. Kid, you're making an old man happy.

geschenk_mag.text: Thank you kindly. Didn't have things like this back then. We gave each other rocks. Nice rocks, mind you.

geschenk_normal.text: Hm. You know what, this is the finest whatsit anyone has ever given me. Word of honor.

text: The thing with the wolf. Right. One night: howling over the hill. The herd nervous, me out with the lantern.
There I stand, heart pounding, and out of the bush comes... the neighbor's pug. With a cold.
His sniffly howling kept three villages awake. I made him tea. That's how you defeat wolves, kid.
Who owned the ranch? Me, kid. Long ago. Every beam here knows my first name.
Then the winters got harder and I got slower. At some point it stood empty. Crushed my heart every day walking past.
And then you came. Now look at her. I'll tell you something: she was waiting for you. So was I, by the way.

tschuess.text: Run along, sprout. I'll stay here and keep an eye on the horizon. Somebody has to.
